title: Experimental Design
purpose: Seed controlled experimental design so Lantern can map testable hypotheses to interventions, comparisons and measurements that support valid inference while respecting feasibility, scope and ethics.

concepts.definition: A designed investigation in which conditions/interventions are deliberately assigned or manipulated to evaluate predictions under explicit assumptions.
The smallest unit independently assigned to a treatment/condition under the design.
A deliberately assigned intervention/exposure/condition.
A comparison condition selected to isolate the effect/question of interest; control need not mean no treatment.
Assignment using a random mechanism to reduce systematic baseline differences and support causal comparison under assumptions.
Sampling from a target population using a random mechanism; distinct from random assignment and primarily related to population generalization.
Withholding condition/allocation information from participants, investigators, assessors or analysts when feasible to reduce specified biases.
A control designed to resemble an intervention except for its hypothesized active component where appropriate.
A measure verifying that an intended manipulation actually changed the targeted intermediate condition.
Measurement before intervention used for description, balance assessment or planned adjustment.
A design varying two or more factors to estimate main effects and interactions efficiently.
The same experimental units experience multiple conditions, requiring attention to order/carryover effects.
Different experimental units receive different conditions.
Units receive multiple treatments in sequence, typically with order/randomization and washout considerations.
Degree to which the design supports the intended causal/inferential conclusion for studied units/conditions.
Degree to which results generalize/transport to other populations, settings, times or conditions.
Degree to which experimental conditions/tasks reflect relevant real-world contexts for the intended inference.
A new application of a study/test intended to assess whether a result reproduces under specified same or varied conditions.
A predeclared rule governing when data collection/analysis stops; important when repeated looks can alter error rates.
Constraints concerning consent, harm, privacy, fairness and acceptable intervention; methodological value does not override ethical boundaries.

guards.reason: Random assignment supports internal causal comparison; it does not make the sample representative.
Random sampling and random assignment solve different problems.
Controls may be active, placebo, usual-care, alternative-treatment or other justified comparisons.
Blinding addresses selected biases but cannot repair all design/measurement/confounding problems.
Randomization reduces systematic bias probabilistically; chance imbalance, noncompliance and implementation problems remain possible.
Showing that manipulation occurred does not establish the predicted downstream outcome.
Strong causal inference in a study does not guarantee transportability/generalization.
Realism/ecological validity does not itself control causal bias.
Reanalysis/republication of the same observations is not independent replication.
Optional stopping/repeated looks can invalidate nominal error rates unless modeled/adjusted.
Expected knowledge gain does not automatically override consent, harm, privacy or other ethical constraints.
Some interventions are impossible/unethical; causal inference may require quasi-experimental or observational methods.

invariants: Experimental design begins from the claim/hypothesis and evidence needed, not from a preferred method.
Random assignment and random sampling are distinct.
Control conditions are chosen to isolate a contrast and need not be untreated.
Blinding addresses specific bias pathways rather than conferring blanket validity.
Internal, external and ecological validity are distinct.
Manipulation checks verify manipulation, not the full hypothesis.
Replication requires a genuinely new evidential application, not mere reuse of the same data.
Stopping/analysis rules should be specified or appropriately modeled when repeated testing affects inference.
Ethical constraints are part of method validity and authority boundaries.
Randomized experiments are powerful but not universally possible, ethical or necessary.

provenance.authoring_basis: Core experimental-design methodology across sciences, including randomization, controls, blinding, validity, replication and ethics, adapted to Lantern's methodology-selection architecture.
